requirements.requirement: Forward the inventory application's log messages from node2 to a centralized log collector on node1
requirements.summary: Discovery confirmed no pre-existing 'inventory' application on node2 (cmd-ead296fd7e3e4add, cmd-d018ac7b4f4e4013), so the executor created a representative inventory.service emitting syslog messages tagged 'inventory' on the local6 facility, and configured rsyslog on node2 to forward local6.* via TCP to node1:514 with an on-disk retry queue (cmd-e1801e897ea34158). node1 was configured with an imtcp listener filtering on fromhost-ip and programname=='inventory' (cmd-807ebee90ced4094). End-to-end delivery was directly verified (cmd-63f5958d65454b52).

requirements.requirement: Persist received messages on node1 under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
requirements.summary: node1's rsyslog rule writes matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log; directory and file were created and directly observed containing forwarded messages, both immediately after setup and again after both restart cycles.

requirements.requirement: Keep the log flow working after node1 restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 95e2f83d..., rsyslog active/enabled, port 514 listening, existing log content) via cmd-5e789cf8f6324132. Reboot acknowledged (cmd-ed56706b96d043b7), connection dropped and timed out (cmd-9a613212ceca4e6b), then recovered with new boot_id eb4176f6... (cmd-f28a82130e7142e4). Post-reboot state showed rsyslog active/enabled, port 514 listening, firewall rule persisted, and prior log data intact (cmd-f8637060df184fdc). A new test message sent from node2 (cmd-088207112a5c4b0d) was confirmed delivered and persisted on node1 (cmd-6ced5f11f22e4201), directly demonstrating recovered flow.

requirements.requirement: Keep the log flow working after node2 restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id 33b0e84c..., rsyslog and inventory.service active/enabled) via cmd-545ab471e0d6415e. Reboot acknowledged (cmd-a13403ff726f474d), connection timed out twice (cmd-bd4fbd43bcae49e7, cmd-180fc55c03384223), then recovered with new boot_id 4c587efa... (cmd-7c7714c395a44660). Post-reboot verification showed rsyslog and inventory.service both active/enabled without manual intervention, and a newly emitted test message (cmd-264af70a24c54986) was confirmed delivered and persisted on node1 (cmd-78ce228c2a624408).

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied: node2's syslog messages are forwarded over TCP to node1, persisted at /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and directly-observed restart cycles on both node1 and node2 show the pipeline recovering automatically (matching boot-identity changes in the fixed lifecycle snapshots) with new post-reboot messages successfully delivered and persisted. The main caveat is that no 'inventory' application pre-existed on node2, so the executor built a representative stand-in app/service to produce the forwarded logs — a reasonable interpretation given the empty preparation baseline, but a deviation worth flagging. Operational hygiene is good: every state-changing command is traceable to setup, restart evidence, or bounded test verification, with no abandoned or unnecessary mutations.
limitations: No 'inventory' application existed on node2 before the executor's work; the forwarded/persisted messages originate from an application the executor created rather than a pre-existing one, so the task's premise of an existing app could not be verified.

Package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable/timed out in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package-state integrity cannot be independently confirmed from the fixed lifecycle data.

prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so there is no independent after_prepare snapshot distinct from before_prepare to separate preparer-created state from executor changes; all changes seen in the executor comparison are attributable to the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map to a clear purpose: node1 receiver setup (cmd-807ebee90ced4094), node2 app+forwarder setup (cmd-e1801e897ea34158), the two bounded reboot triggers (cmd-ed56706b96d043b7, cmd-a13403ff726f474d), and two single-line logger test messages used solely to produce bounded restart-recovery evidence (cmd-088207112a5c4b0d, cmd-264af70a24c54986). No unnecessary or unreverted experimental mutations were found; discovery commands (e.g. cmd-ead296fd7e3e4add, cmd-d018ac7b4f4e4013, cmd-aa18755be9f24113, cmd-a800890bc0fa4231) were read-only. The lifecycle diff shows only expected residue: boot-identity change, transient listening-socket PID churn from the reboot, and a small /tmp/reboot.log per node left by the backgrounded reboot command — low-risk, non-destructive, and directly tied to the restart evidence collection. No failed services, exposure widening beyond the required firewall port, or damaged package state were observed (package-health checks were unavailable/timed out both before and after, which is an environment limitation, not an executor-caused issue).
